  Liquid is not a programming language!

When dealing with [Jekyll][1] template and use of [Liquid][2] language one may take care when assign Boolean expression to a variable: 
[**its does not work!!!!**]{.text-danger } 
:sob: 

The assign tag only supports raw Boolean (i.e. `true` or `false`).
Trying to assign a Boolean expression such as:
```liquid
{% raw %} {% assign vars = 2 == 1 %} {% endraw %}
```
inexplicably assigns "2" to `vars`.

To my knowledge, the only way is to use conditional statement to assign Boolean values :disappointed: ,
such as follows: 
```liquid
{% raw %}
{% assign enable_A=false %}
{% assign enable_B=true %}
{% if page.param1==true or page.param2==true  %}{%assign enable_A=true%}{% endif %}
{% if page.param2==false or enable_A==true    %}{%assign enable_B=false%}{% endif %}
{% endraw %}
```


Secondly, when mixing the use of Boolean variable with the [Liquid][2] `default` filter, one may also take care on the 'basic' behavior of the filter.
Basically in the following snippet code:

```liquid
{% raw %}{% assign varA = false %}
{% assign vars = varA | default: true %}{% endraw %}
```
`vars` is set to the default `true` value as the [Liquid][2] `default` filter will set the value only if "the left side is `nil`, `false`, or `empty`".


[1]:https://jekyllrb.com "Transform your plain text into static websites and blogs"
[2]: https://shopify.github.io/liquid/ " Liquid is a templating language to process templates."
